title: Limited L2 orderbook does not produce consistent amount of results - CCXT PRO
body:
- OS: Win10
- Programming Language version: Python 3.8
- CCXT version: 0.0.47
- Exchange: Binance, WS

```
import ccxtpro
import asyncio

async def main():
    exchange = ccxtpro.binance({'enableRateLimit': True})
    while True:
        orderbook = await exchange.watch_order_book('ETH/BTC', 10) #INCONSISTENT, see below
        print(len(orderbook['asks']), len(orderbook['bids']))

asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(main())

```

Results:

```
10 10
10 10
10 9
9 10
10 10
10 10
10 10
10 9
10 10
```

and:
```
        orderbook = await exchange.watch_order_book('ETH/BTC', 1)
        print(orderbook['asks'][0]), (orderbook['bids'][0])
```
Produces (after some correct results):
```
    print(orderbook['asks'][0]), (orderbook['bids'][0])
IndexError: list index out of range
```
author: 1key

comments.body:
Technically, this is not fully a bug. What happens is that when you limit the orders in real-time mode by supplying the `limit` argument CCXT will only store up to `limit` orders. In some cases an order may be deleted from the book (when matched), so the exchange sends a zero delta and it is removed from the orderbook leaving just the 9 orders of 10 (until another one fills the gap). The responsibility of CCXT Pro in this case is to return immediately after receiving a "delete" command from the exchange (or any of "delete", "update", "insert" deltas).

So, from here, you have two options:

- either expect the number of bids/asks to be less than or equal to `limit` in the result 
- or don't send `limit` (CCXT will keep the entire orderbook in memory) and just use python's array slicing like `[0:5]`

Also, Binance does support limited WS feeds for 5, 10 or 20 bidasks, however, when `limit` is sent to the exchange – it will rate-limit the feed by 100ms or 1000ms which is not good for real-time apps, therefore the `limit` is not sent to Binance in particular at this time, and all the limiting is done on the client-side in memory.

We will add this to the documentation shortly to avoid confusion.

Let me know if that does not answer the question.

Clear and fast answer!
Will work around it then.

@1key we will look into adding an option that would still store the entire orderbook and would always serve a number of bidasks as close as possible to `limit` , but in the general case an exchange orderbook may have less than any number of bid/asks (just like with fetchOrderBook over REST). So if the exchange is inactive, there may be very few or even zero orders on either side of the book. 

Feel free to reopen this if anything or just ask further questions if you have more. Thanks for the feedback!

satisfaction_conditions: A clear explanation of why the orderbook sometimes returns fewer results than the requested limit
Practical workarounds or alternatives to handle the inconsistent number of results
Transparency about the current implementation's behavior and limitations

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

dockerfile:
FROM python:3.8-slim

# Install system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Clone the repository with depth 1 to save space
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt.git . && \
    git fetch --depth 1 origin a9103f7702ced45e6448a5afd62871b194843b06 && \
    git checkout a9103f7702ced45e6448a5afd62871b194843b06

# Install Python dependencies
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir \
    aiohttp \
    aiodns \
    cchardet \
    yarl \
    cryptography \
    websockets \
    setuptools

# Set up Python path for ccxt
ENV PYTHONPATH="${PYTHONPATH}:/app"

# Create a directory for credentials
RUN mkdir -p /app/ccxtpro-credentials

# Create test script directory
RUN mkdir -p /app/test

# Create a sample test script file
RUN echo 'import ccxtpro\nimport asyncio\n\nasync def main():\n    exchange = ccxtpro.binance({\"enableRateLimit\": True})\n    orderbook = await exchange.watch_order_book(\"ETH/BTC\", 10)\n    print(len(orderbook[\"asks\"]), len(orderbook[\"bids\"]))\n    await exchange.close()\n\nasyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(main())' > /app/test/test_orderbook.py

# Create a README with instructions
RUN echo "# CCXT Pro Test Environment\n\n" \
    "This container provides an environment for testing CCXT Pro with the Binance exchange.\n\n" \
    "## Instructions:\n" \
    "1. Install CCXT Pro with your credentials:\n" \
    "   pip install git+https://YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN@github.com/ccxt/ccxt.pro.git#subdirectory=python\n\n" \
    "2. Run the test script:\n" \
    "   python /app/test/test_orderbook.py\n" > /app/README.md

WORKDIR /app

CMD ["cat", "/app/README.md"]
